tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in messages from the system in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

Required unless `stop` is true.

Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a message from the system confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a message from the system confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

3	## 1. 本讲目标
4	
5	这是学习手册的收官之讲。前面八讲我们把 fast-ulysses 的每一层都拆开看过——plan、窗口、传输、屏障、算子注册、异步路径、构建与测试。本讲换一个视角：**不再问「它是怎么工作的」，而问「它站在什么之上、它放弃了什么」**。

14

16	
17	本讲几乎不引入新机制，但要求你带着前几讲的结论来读：
18	
19	- **CE（copy engine，拷贝引擎）**：GPU 上独立于流式多核（SM）的 DMA 拷贝单元。远端 peer 拷贝走 CE、不占 SM（u5-l1、u5-l2）。
20	- **release/acquire 内存序**：`red.release.sys` 与 `ld.acquire.sys` 这对 PTX 指令构成发布-等待协议——release 之前的写对拿到对应 acquire 读的线程可见（u5-l3）。
21	- **两道屏障**：每次调用是「开路屏障 → CE 传输 → 收尾屏障」三段式。开路屏障让写者等读者（单缓冲窗口保护），收尾屏障向全组宣布「我写的字节已落地」（u6-l2）。

45	### 4.1 未文档化的假设：CE 写入何时对目的地可见
46	
47	#### 4.1.1 概念说明
48	
49	整个 fast-ulysses 只依赖一条没有任何厂商文档保证的性质。design.md 把它写成一句加粗的话：
50	
51	> **A completed copy-engine write is visible at the destination by the time a later kernel's release store announcing it arrives.**
52	> （一次已完成的拷贝引擎写入，在随后某个内核为它发布的那条 release store 到达目的地之前，就已经对目的地可见。）
53	
54	它为什么是命门？看一次调用的时序：rank $r$ 用 `cudaMemcpy2D/3DAsync` 把字节写进各 peer 的窗口（CE 干的），然后启动收尾屏障内核，内核里的 `red.release.sys` 向每个 peer 的 `flags[r]` 发布本轮 epoch；peer $t$ 的内核用 `ld.acquire.sys` 自旋等自己的 `flags[r]$ 达到该 epoch，等到了就去读窗口。release/acquire 这一对（PTX 有定义）保证了「release 之前的写」对「拿到同步的 acquire 读」可见。**问题是：CE 写入是不是「release 之前的写」？** PTX 对 `.release` 的作用域定义是「当前线程的先前操作」——而 CE 传输不是任何线程的操作，它是主机通过流提交的 DMA。于是链条里有一环是空的，而整个设计踩在这一环上。
55	
56	注意边界：这条假设**只关乎收尾屏障**。开路屏障（写者等读者）保护的是单缓冲窗口，不涉及「CE 写是否落地」；出问题的方向只有一个——发布者宣布了、字节还在路上。也注意它是**可见性**假设而不是序假设：流序保证内核在拷贝之后启动（这是主机侧语义），悬而未决的只是「内核启动时，目的地能不能读到那些字节」。

146	### 4.2 NCCL 的替代形状：让 flag 与数据同乘一台引擎
147	
148	#### 4.2.1 概念说明
149	
150	面对同一条假设，业界有两条路：**接受它并加强发布**（本库、NVSHMEM、TransformerEngine——只是加强的程度不同），或者**换一个形状让它不再被需要**。NCCL 2.28+ 的 kernel-less CE 集合通信（`ce_coll.cc`、`NCCL_CTA_POLICY_ZERO`）选了后者：flag 不是由 SM 内核发布的，而是**一次 8 字节的 device-to-device `cudaMemcpyAsync`，与 payload 同流、同引擎**，随后用 `cuStreamWaitValue32` 在流上等待。于是「CE 写 → 内核 release」这条无人担保的边被替换成「同一台 CE 上同流的两次拷贝」——flag 与数据走同一条路，先后到达由引擎内部的流序兜住，假设从「跨引擎跨执行单元的可见性」退化为「一台引擎对自己的队列的序」，后者即便同样没有正式文档，风险面也小得多。
151	
152	design.md 的态度很克制：**「That is the shape to move to if this assumption ever has to go」**——这是假设破产时的逃生方向，不是现在的选择。为什么不现在就搬？因为作者实测过这条形状的两个构件，两个都更慢。
153	
154	#### 4.2.2 核心流程
155	
156	把「NCCL 形状的收尾握手」与现状并排：
157	
158	```text
159	现状（barrier kernel）：
160	  xfer 流:  [CE payload 拷贝...] → (join 事件) → caller 流: [K_close: red.release.sys × ws] → [K_open/spin]
161	  发布者 = SM 内核（1 次启动，4–6 µs）
162	  等待者 = SM 内核（自旋）
163	
164	NCCL 形状：
165	  同一条流: [CE payload 拷贝...] → [CE 8B flag D2D 拷贝 × ws] → cuStreamWaitValue32(每个 peer 的 flag)
166	  发布者 = CE（7 次 8B peer 拷贝 ≈ 16 µs，ws=8）
167	  等待者 = 流 memop（对调度器不可见）
168	```
169	
170	两条实测代价（design.md「The barrier」章 + benchmark.md 被否决方案表）：
171	
172	1. **发布侧更慢**：把收尾 flag 改成传输流上的 CE 写（NCCL 的 kernel-less 形状），实测比它要替换的屏障内核**慢 3×**——ws=8 时 7 次 8 字节 peer 拷贝约 16 µs，对内核的 4–6 µs；而且它只挪走了「发布」，等待仍在内核里。
173	2. **等待侧在并发计算下更差**：`cuStreamWriteValue64/WaitValue64` 实测把并发 GEMM 下的重叠从 **+34% 拉到 −28%**——恰是本算子存在的理由的反面。CUDA memop 文档给出了机制：经这些 API 建立的序「对 CUDA 不可见」，被阻塞的 memop 在工作调度器眼里不存在，并发内核会被排在它后面。
174	
175	另有一段**自我修正**值得细读：早期版本的 design.md 曾把回归归咎于 `CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_CAN_FLUSH_REMOTE_WRITES`，后来查实该属性只门控 `_FLUSH` 变体（那是给 NIC 经 PCIe 到达的写准备的）；NVSHMEM 的 on-stream 等待确实需要它并使用 `FLUSH`，而 **NCCL 的 CE 等待两者都不用**——所以该属性本身并不构成「等待形式在 NVLink 上不可用」的理由，**实测回归才是**。

214	### 4.3 为何拒绝 PCIe：不稳定比慢更致命
215	
216	#### 4.3.1 概念说明
217	
218	「为什么只有 NVLink」不是一个偏好问题，而是一个实测结论加一个工程决策：
219	
220	- **实测结论**：在 PCIe 上本算子**正确但更慢**，且慢的倍数不稳定——跨 CPU socket 时，一台 PCIe 节点上跑出基线的 0.62×，另一台 0.14×，两台相差 5 倍，因此**不做平均**。
221	- **工程决策**：要在这拓扑上追平 NCCL，需要一条「共享主机内存传输 + 第二次握手」——那是一个**新传输层**，不是调度改动，且在 NVLink 上一文不值。既然不建，就**让构造函数拒绝这个拓扑，而不是假装支持**。
222	
223	关键的分析转折是「fabric 不是差异所在」：两台节点上平坦的 peer 拷贝都能到同样的带宽（单流 54.6 / 55.9 GB/s，八路并发每流 52.1 GB/s），差异在于**带步长（pitched）的拷贝模式能从 fabric 里抽取多少**——一台 11.2 GB/s、一台 2.1 GB/s，即同一上限的 20% 与 4%，而 NVLink 机器上是 90–99%。也就是说，本库「重排即步长」的核心换法（u1-l1、u3-l2）在 PCIe 交换机的布线方式面前失效了，且失效程度取决于 socket 之下 PCIe switch 的具体布局（快的那台 2+2 成对，慢的那台 3+1）。传输段本身成了慢的那一段——与 NVLink 上的情形正好相反，「步长换重排」的交易在那里不再划算。

342	**答案**：因为 peer 的 flag 地址按值装在 `BarPeers::p[8]`（[src/barrier.cu:L27-L29](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/src/barrier.cu#L27-L29)）这个定长数组里随内核参数传入。放宽至少要改成指针+长度（或 `cudaMemcpyToSymbol` 到常量/全局内存），并同步放宽算子层 `[1,8]` 校验；但单节点 8 卡的物理上限让它不值得——这正是「结构事实」类边界与「待办」的区别。
343	
344	## 5. 综合实践
345	
346	**任务：写一篇 300 字左右的设计评审笔记——《如果把屏障换成 NCCL 形状》**。这是全手册最后一个实践，也是规格指定的本讲实践任务，它把 4.1 的假设、4.2 的形状、4.4 的评审文体串成一份真实可用的工程文档。
347	
348	**要求**：
349	
350	1. **改动清单**：列出四个必改文件及各自改动——
351	   - [src/barrier.cu](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/src/barrier.cu)：`fast_barrier` 拆分——发布改为在 xfer 流上向每个 peer 的 `flags[rank]` 发 8 字节 D2D 拷贝；等待改为 `cuStreamWaitValue32`；自旋内核退役（`BarPeers` 可留作地址载体）。
352	   - [src/transfer.cu](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/src/transfer.cu)：flag 拷贝必须排在 `launch_a2a_ce` 已发射的 peer 拷贝**同一条 xfer 流**之后（「同引擎」是规避假设的全部意义）；故障注入的 join 跳过分支语义随之复核。
353	   - [include/fast_ulysses/transfer.hpp](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/include/fast_ulysses/transfer.hpp)：契约注释改写——握手区布局从「`uint64 flags[ws]` + `uint64 epoch`」改为 32 位 flag 的约定（`cuStreamWaitValue32` 是 32 位等待），`fast_barrier` 的签名与文档同步。
354	   - [src/group.cc](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/src/group.cc)：[L18-L37](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/src/group.cc#L18-L37) 的 `flag_slots`/`flag_offset_slots` 与 [L250](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/src/group.cc#L250) 的清零范围按新布局重算，signal pad 末尾的偏移不变、宽度变。
355	2. **代价**（必须引 design.md 论证过的两条）：发布侧 3× 慢（7×8B ≈ 16 µs vs 内核 4–6 µs，且只挪发布）；等待侧 memop 在并发 GEMM 下把重叠 +34% 拖到 −28%（「序对 CUDA 不可见」）。
356	3. **开放问题至少一条**：`cuStreamWriteValue32` 的写值与 `cuStreamWaitValue32` 的比较值都是主机参数、图捕获时固化——与「epoch 必须由设备侧 `atomicAdd` 推进，否则重放被陈旧状态满足」（[src/barrier.cu:L33-L37](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/src/barrier.cu#L33-L37)、[docs/design.md:L85-L89](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/docs/design.md#L85-L89)）如何相容？design.md 未回答——评审笔记的价值就在于把它写出来。

359	   - 无注意力内核 → 「qkv 打包进 `3*head_dim` 末维、两次调用之间放你自己的 SDPA，照 [examples/dit_attention.py](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/examples/dit_attention.py) 的三明治组装。」
360	   - 3D/5D 入口不存在 → 「上游按 `(b, s, n, d)` 投影：5D 折 qkv 轴成 `(b, s, n, 3d)`（警惕 4.4 之外的混头陷阱），`(s, n, d)` 补一个 view。」
361	
362	**预期结果**：一篇你自己的、可放进团队 wiki 的评审短文——有改动清单、有引证代价、有开放问题、有迁移对策。**参考答案不提供全文**（抄结论就失去了评审训练），只提供自检三条：① 四个文件是否都出现且改动与 4.2.3 的源码事实一致；② 两条代价是否带数字与出处；③ 开放问题是否触及「固化进图」这个 design.md 未覆盖的角落。全部纯纸面作业，无需 GPU。
363	
364	## 6. 本讲小结
365	
366	- **一条假设撑起整个库**：「已完成的 CE 写在随后内核的 release store 到达前对目的地可见」——四份权威（API Reference 的主机侧完成语义、Programming Guide 的 NULL 流限定、PTX 的线程作用域、全体厂商的沉默）全部不给背书；业界三家接受它（NVSHMEM、TE 更弱，本库至少带 release），NCCL 换形状规避它。
367	- **实证不等于证明**：`ce_ordering.py` 每次运行武装负控制，`armed > 0 and torn == 0` 才算数——证据的效力以「测试还能失败」为前提。
368	- **NCCL 形状是逃生口不是现答案**：flag 走 D2D 拷贝同流同引擎 + `cuStreamWaitValue32` 等待；实测发布侧 3× 慢、等待侧把并发重叠从 +34% 拖到 −28%（memop 的序对 CUDA 不可见）；且 `CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_CAN_FLUSH_REMOTE_WRITES` 已被作者自我修正为「不是理由」。
369	- **拒绝 PCIe 靠的是不稳定的实测**：0.62×/0.14×、两节点 5× 分歧不做平均；fabric 相同（平坦拷贝带宽一致），垮掉的是跨步模式的抽取率（20%/4% vs 90–99%），随 switch 布局漂移；追平需要新传输层而不建，于是构造函数拒绝而非假装。
370	- **「删过的表面」各有判词**：NVSHMEM（torch 对称内存全盘接替）、借出入口（`out=`+`empty_output` 把寿命还给调用者）、`tag`（无歧义可消）、`reserve/seal`（死锁的食物没了）、回退组（用 torch.distributed 才是答案）——外加结构性的 `BarPeers::p[8]`、单节点、无注意力内核。
371	- **design.md 本身会修订自己**：CAN_FLUSH 一段与 v0.1 的「跨步从不慢于平坦」被后来的测量推翻——设计文档是活文本，这是它可信的原因。
372	
373	## 7. 下一步学习建议
374	
375	本讲到此，九个单元全部完成。三条收束路线：
376	
377	1. **把手册读到代码里去**：挑一个你真正关心的改动（比如综合实践的 NCCL 形状，或双缓冲窗口——benchmark.md 记录它只值 ~0.7% 且会摧毁 window_race 的前提），在仓库里追一遍它会触碰的每个文件，用本手册各讲的调用链图核对；给别人讲一遍 4.1 的四条缺位，讲不清的地方就是你要重读的地方。
378	2. **去读被对照的实现**：NCCL 的 `ce_coll.cc`（kernel-less CE 路径）、NVSHMEM 的 `signal_op` 回退内核、TransformerEngine 的 `ring_exchange`——design.md 对它们只各用了一句，值得带着本讲的框架去看原仓库里那句话的实物。
379	3. **带着这套方法论看下一个项目**：每当代码「能跑」时问三个问题——它依赖哪条没人写下来的性质（4.1）？它拒绝的边界在哪、依据是实测还是偏好（4.3）？它删掉了什么、接替者的不变量是否更强（4.4）？这三个问题就是这本手册想留给你的东西。

# 设计反思：未文档化的假设与被删掉的方案

## 1. 本讲目标

这是学习手册的收官之讲。前面八讲我们把 fast-ulysses 的每一层都拆开看过——plan、窗口、传输、屏障、算子注册、异步路径、构建与测试。本讲换一个视角：**不再问「它是怎么工作的」，而问「它站在什么之上、它放弃了什么」**。

学完后你应该能够：

1. 一字不差地陈述本项目赖以生存的核心假设——「一次已完成的拷贝引擎（CE）写入，会在随后 announce 它的内核 release store 到达之前，对目的地可见」——并说出支持「没有任何厂商文档保证它」这一判断的四条具体理由。
2. 复述 NCCL 如何用「换形状」规避这条假设，以及 design.md 论证过的、为什么本库不照搬的两条实测代价。
3. 复述拒绝 PCIe 的实测依据：两个节点 0.62× 与 0.14×、相差 5 倍且不做平均；瓶颈不在 fabric 而在跨步拷贝模式对 fabric 的抽取率。
4. 对 design.md「Removed, and why」清单里的每个被删特性，各用一句话说出删除理由，并把它们与 migration.md 的「本项目没有的东西」对上号。
5. 写出一篇有理有据的设计评审笔记：如果要把屏障换成 NCCL 形状，要动哪些文件、付出什么代价、留下什么没回答的问题。

## 2. 前置知识

本讲几乎不引入新机制，但要求你带着前几讲的结论来读：

- **CE（copy engine，拷贝引擎）**：GPU 上独立于流式多核（SM）的 DMA 拷贝单元。远端 peer 拷贝走 CE、不占 SM（u5-l1、u5-l2）。
- **release/acquire 内存序**：`red.release.sys` 与 `ld.acquire.sys` 这对 PTX 指令构成发布-等待协议——release 之前的写对拿到对应 acquire 读的线程可见（u5-l3）。
- **两道屏障**：每次调用是「开路屏障 → CE 传输 → 收尾屏障」三段式。开路屏障让写者等读者（单缓冲窗口保护），收尾屏障向全组宣布「我写的字节已落地」（u6-l2）。
- **设备侧 epoch**：轮次计数由 `atomicAdd` 在内核里推进，而不是主机算好传进去——为了让 CUDA graph 重放不满足于陈旧状态（u5-l3）。
- **负控制（negative control）**：故意注入故障、确认测试还能失败，否则测试「变盲」——证明不了任何东西（u9-l3）。
- **SPMD 契约**：所有 rank 发出相同的调用序列，违反的后果是挂起而非报错（u1-l2、u4-l2）。

一个值得先建立的直觉：**「正确」有两层**。一层是「在我测过的机器上每次都对」；另一层是「有文档或规范背书，换一台机器、换一个驱动版本仍然对」。fast-ulysses 的作者在 design.md 里极其诚实地区分了这两层，并把第一层里最危险的一条单独拎出来写成一章——这就是本讲 4.1 的主角。

## 3. 本讲源码地图

| 文件 | 作用 |
| --- | --- |
| [docs/design.md](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/docs/design.md) | 本讲的主文本：「What this rests on that is not documented」「Why NVLink only」「Removed, and why」三章 |
| [docs/migration.md](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/docs/migration.md) | 从 DeepSpeed / sglang / yunchang 迁移的对照表，以及「What this does not have」清单 |
| [src/barrier.cu](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/src/barrier.cu) | 自旋屏障内核：release/acquire PTX、设备侧 epoch、`BarPeers::p[8]` |
| [src/transfer.cu](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/src/transfer.cu) | CE 传输路径，以及测试专用故障注入 `set_ce_fault` |
| [include/fast_ulysses/transfer.hpp](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/include/fast_ulysses/transfer.hpp) | 屏障与故障注入的契约注释（握手区布局写在这里） |
| [src/group.cc](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/src/group.cc) | 握手区在 signal pad 末尾的布局计算（评审「换形状」时要动的第四处） |
| [src/nvlink.cc](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/src/nvlink.cc) | `check_nvlink`：fail-open 语义与拒绝始末 |
| [python/fast_ulysses/group.py](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/python/fast_ulysses/group.py) | `_require_nvlink`：设备号 all_gather 后调用 C++ 检查 |
| [test/distributed/ce_ordering.py](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/test/distributed/ce_ordering.py) | 假设的实证测试 + 每次运行都武装的负控制 |
| [docs/benchmark.md](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/docs/benchmark.md) | "Why not PCIe" 一章的实测数字；被否决替代方案表 |

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

### 4.1 未文档化的假设：CE 写入何时对目的地可见

#### 4.1.1 概念说明

整个 fast-ulysses 只依赖一条没有任何厂商文档保证的性质。design.md 把它写成一句加粗的话：

> **A completed copy-engine write is visible at the destination by the time a later kernel's release store announcing it arrives.**
> （一次已完成的拷贝引擎写入，在随后某个内核为它发布的那条 release store 到达目的地之前，就已经对目的地可见。）

它为什么是命门？看一次调用的时序：rank $r$ 用 `cudaMemcpy2D/3DAsync` 把字节写进各 peer 的窗口（CE 干的），然后启动收尾屏障内核，内核里的 `red.release.sys` 向每个 peer 的 `flags[r]` 发布本轮 epoch；peer $t$ 的内核用 `ld.acquire.sys` 自旋等自己的 `flags[r]$ 达到该 epoch，等到了就去读窗口。release/acquire 这一对（PTX 有定义）保证了「release 之前的写」对「拿到同步的 acquire 读」可见。**问题是：CE 写入是不是「release 之前的写」？** PTX 对 `.release` 的作用域定义是「当前线程的先前操作」——而 CE 传输不是任何线程的操作，它是主机通过流提交的 DMA。于是链条里有一环是空的，而整个设计踩在这一环上。

注意边界：这条假设**只关乎收尾屏障**。开路屏障（写者等读者）保护的是单缓冲窗口，不涉及「CE 写是否落地」；出问题的方向只有一个——发布者宣布了、字节还在路上。也注意它是**可见性**假设而不是序假设：流序保证内核在拷贝之后启动（这是主机侧语义），悬而未决的只是「内核启动时，目的地能不能读到那些字节」。

#### 4.1.2 核心流程

把一次收尾握手里各事件的依赖画出来，标注每一环的依据：

\[
\underbrace{W_{r\to t}}_{\text{CE 写入}} \;\prec_{\text{stream}}\; \underbrace{K_r}_{\text{收尾内核}} \;\prec_{\text{release.sys}}\; \underbrace{F_t[r]=e}_{\text{flag 发布}} \;\prec_{\text{acquire.sys}}\; \underbrace{K_t\ \text{自旋退出}}_{\text{读到 } e} \;\prec\; \underbrace{R_{t}}_{\text{读窗口}}
\]

- $\prec_{\text{stream}}$：流序说内核在拷贝「完成」之后才启动——但 CUDA API 对 memcpy「完成」的定义是**主机侧性质**（何时向主机报告完成），不是「对目的设备可见」。
- $\prec_{\text{release.sys}} / \prec_{\text{acquire.sys}}$：PTX 有定义，但 release 只序「当前线程的先前操作」，CE 传输不在内。
- 于是 $W_{r\to t} \Rightarrow R_t$ 这条端到端可见性，四份权威文档全部缺席：

| # | 文档缺位 | 原文依据（design.md「What this rests on that is not documented」） |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | CUDA API Reference | memcpy 的「完成」被定义为主机侧性质，不含目的地可见性 |
| 2 | CUDA Programming Guide | 跨设备序保证只覆盖 NULL 流，且对非默认流上的异步拷贝明确撤回 |
| 3 | PTX | `.release` 的作用域是「当前线程的先前操作」，CE 传输不是线程的操作 |
| 4 | 全体厂商文档 | 没有任何一方对这条序给出任一方向的文档 |

作者同时给出了业界对照，用来校准「该多担心」：

| 实现者 | 形状 | 序强度 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **NVSHMEM** | on-stream `signal_op`：CE 送 payload，然后由 `<<<1,1>>>` 内核裸 `atomicAdd_system` 发 flag，**无任何 fence** | 比本库**更弱** |
| **TransformerEngine** | userbuffers 的 `ring_exchange`（出货默认）同样形状 | 比本库**更弱** |
| **本库** | 收尾屏障用 `red.release.sys` 发布 | 至少带了 release |
| **NCCL** | kernel-less CE 集合通信（2.28+）：flag 作为 8 字节 D2D 拷贝与 payload 同流同引擎，`cuStreamWaitValue32` 等待 | **换形状规避**（见 4.2） |

最后是证据与保证的区分：「It holds in testing, which is evidence and not a guarantee」——`ce_ordering.py` 每次运行都武装负控制，让这条实证不会悄悄变成不测试任何东西的空转。

#### 4.1.3 源码精读

### 4.2 NCCL 的替代形状：让 flag 与数据同乘一台引擎

#### 4.2.1 概念说明

面对同一条假设，业界有两条路：**接受它并加强发布**（本库、NVSHMEM、TransformerEngine——只是加强的程度不同），或者**换一个形状让它不再被需要**。NCCL 2.28+ 的 kernel-less CE 集合通信（`ce_coll.cc`、`NCCL_CTA_POLICY_ZERO`）选了后者：flag 不是由 SM 内核发布的，而是**一次 8 字节的 device-to-device `cudaMemcpyAsync`，与 payload 同流、同引擎**，随后用 `cuStreamWaitValue32` 在流上等待。于是「CE 写 → 内核 release」这条无人担保的边被替换成「同一台 CE 上同流的两次拷贝」——flag 与数据走同一条路，先后到达由引擎内部的流序兜住，假设从「跨引擎跨执行单元的可见性」退化为「一台引擎对自己的队列的序」，后者即便同样没有正式文档，风险面也小得多。

design.md 的态度很克制：**「That is the shape to move to if this assumption ever has to go」**——这是假设破产时的逃生方向，不是现在的选择。为什么不现在就搬？因为作者实测过这条形状的两个构件，两个都更慢。

#### 4.2.2 核心流程

把「NCCL 形状的收尾握手」与现状并排：

```text
现状（barrier kernel）：
  xfer 流:  [CE payload 拷贝...] → (join 事件) → caller 流: [K_close: red.release.sys × ws] → [K_open/spin]
  发布者 = SM 内核（1 次启动，4–6 µs）
  等待者 = SM 内核（自旋）

NCCL 形状：
  同一条流: [CE payload 拷贝...] → [CE 8B flag D2D 拷贝 × ws] → cuStreamWaitValue32(每个 peer 的 flag)
  发布者 = CE（7 次 8B peer 拷贝 ≈ 16 µs，ws=8）
  等待者 = 流 memop（对调度器不可见）
```

两条实测代价（design.md「The barrier」章 + benchmark.md 被否决方案表）：

1. **发布侧更慢**：把收尾 flag 改成传输流上的 CE 写（NCCL 的 kernel-less 形状），实测比它要替换的屏障内核**慢 3×**——ws=8 时 7 次 8 字节 peer 拷贝约 16 µs，对内核的 4–6 µs；而且它只挪走了「发布」，等待仍在内核里。
2. **等待侧在并发计算下更差**：`cuStreamWriteValue64/WaitValue64` 实测把并发 GEMM 下的重叠从 **+34% 拉到 −28%**——恰是本算子存在的理由的反面。CUDA memop 文档给出了机制：经这些 API 建立的序「对 CUDA 不可见」，被阻塞的 memop 在工作调度器眼里不存在，并发内核会被排在它后面。

另有一段**自我修正**值得细读：早期版本的 design.md 曾把回归归咎于 `CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_CAN_FLUSH_REMOTE_WRITES`，后来查实该属性只门控 `_FLUSH` 变体（那是给 NIC 经 PCIe 到达的写准备的）；NVSHMEM 的 on-stream 等待确实需要它并使用 `FLUSH`，而 **NCCL 的 CE 等待两者都不用**——所以该属性本身并不构成「等待形式在 NVLink 上不可用」的理由，**实测回归才是**。

### 4.3 为何拒绝 PCIe：不稳定比慢更致命

#### 4.3.1 概念说明

「为什么只有 NVLink」不是一个偏好问题，而是一个实测结论加一个工程决策：

- **实测结论**：在 PCIe 上本算子**正确但更慢**，且慢的倍数不稳定——跨 CPU socket 时，一台 PCIe 节点上跑出基线的 0.62×，另一台 0.14×，两台相差 5 倍，因此**不做平均**。
- **工程决策**：要在这拓扑上追平 NCCL，需要一条「共享主机内存传输 + 第二次握手」——那是一个**新传输层**，不是调度改动，且在 NVLink 上一文不值。既然不建，就**让构造函数拒绝这个拓扑，而不是假装支持**。

关键的分析转折是「fabric 不是差异所在」：两台节点上平坦的 peer 拷贝都能到同样的带宽（单流 54.6 / 55.9 GB/s，八路并发每流 52.1 GB/s），差异在于**带步长（pitched）的拷贝模式能从 fabric 里抽取多少**——一台 11.2 GB/s、一台 2.1 GB/s，即同一上限的 20% 与 4%，而 NVLink 机器上是 90–99%。也就是说，本库「重排即步长」的核心换法（u1-l1、u3-l2）在 PCIe 交换机的布线方式面前失效了，且失效程度取决于 socket 之下 PCIe switch 的具体布局（快的那台 2+2 成对，慢的那台 3+1）。传输段本身成了慢的那一段——与 NVLink 上的情形正好相反，「步长换重排」的交易在那里不再划算。

#### 4.3.2 核心流程

拒绝链路（谁在哪儿拒绝）：

```text
UlyssesGroup(require_nvlink=True)
  └─ python/fast_ulysses/group.py: _require_nvlink
       ├─ all_gather 各 rank 的设备号          ← 保证全组结论一致（拒绝必须集体发生）
       ├─ 两 rank 共占一 GPU → 跳过检查         ← 不是本检查关心的拓扑
       └─ _C.check_nvlink(devices)
            └─ src/nvlink.cc: check_nvlink
                 ├─ nvlink_matrix 返回 nullopt → 返回空串（fail-open：说不出就放行）
                 └─ 矩阵确有 false 对 → 返回拒绝消息 → Python raise RuntimeError
```

benchmark.md 还记录了这条拒绝链的实机验证：在一台全无 NVLink 的机器上，默认构造抛出 `cuda:0 and cuda:1 are not joined by NVLink`，`doctor` 打印全 `N` 矩阵，而同一台机器 `pytest test/` 51/51 通过（测试显式关掉检查构造组）——**拒绝生效，且不影响其余正确性**。

### 4.4 被移除的表面：每条一句话的理由

#### 4.4.1 概念说明

design.md 的最后一章「Removed, and why」开篇一句是全文的座右铭：**「Earlier versions carried more surface than they could defend」**——早期版本背着超过自己能辩护能力的 API 表面。删除不是做减法的审美，而是把每条表面要么换成**有更强不变量支撑的等价物**，要么确认**它要防的问题已经不存在**。这张清单是理解当前 API 形状（u2、u4 学过的 `out=`、`empty_output`、`lend`）为什么长成这样的反面教材：你知道了它们取代了什么，才算真正知道它们是什么。

与它互补的是 migration.md 的「What this does not have」——那不是「删过」的历史，而是**现存的边界**，迁移前先读：「Check this list before you start, not after」。

#### 4.4.2 核心流程

五条被删特性 → 一句话理由 → 接替者：

| 被删掉的 | 一句话理由 | 接替者 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **NVSHMEM 后端** | 它给的正是 torch 对称内存后来给的（带 peer 地址的 VMM 分配），代价却是一整套 bootstrap、按步长切 team、独立池分配器、两个为躲开 torch 自带 NVSHMEM 符号冲突而挑的未文档化 `hostlib_` 入口、外加一条无法执行的「活组必须瓜分作业」规则——换到 torch 后**无一存活** | `empty_strided_p2p` + `rendezvous`（u4-l1） |
| **借出窗口的入口点**（结果即窗口本身） | 生命周期契约没有任何机制强制，谁也说不清缓冲何时被回收 | `out=` 接 `empty_output()`：同样的节省，缓冲寿命握在调用者手里（u4-l3） |
| **`tag` 参数** | 它为了「同时存活的结果分居不同窗口」而存在；拷贝路径每次调用各自新张量、零拷贝路径用调用者自己的缓冲，**已无歧义可消** | 无（问题消失） |
| **`reserve()` / `seal()`** | 它们防的是旧池「分配是集合的且流同步」导致的调用中途死锁；那死锁的食物——一次故意留在飞行中的自旋屏障——随延迟收尾握手一起被删，死锁饿死了 | 无（死锁源头已除） |
| **`torch.distributed` 回退组** | 对不该支持的拓扑提供回退等于假装支持；正确的答案是「直接用 torch.distributed」 | 构造期 NVLink 拒绝（4.3） |

「What this does not have」清单里值得单独点名的三条（它们是**结构事实**而非删除历史）：

- **跨节点**：没有任何字节走 NIC。
- **`world_size > 8`**：结构性的——`BarPeers::p[8]`（[src/barrier.cu:L27-L29](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/src/barrier.cu#L27-L29)），peer 地址按值传进内核的定长数组。

#### 4.4.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：`tag` 被删是因为「没什么可消歧的了」。用 u4 的知识解释：哪两条路径让「同时存活的结果分居不同窗口」不再必要？

**答案**：拷贝路径（默认）每次调用都产出自己的新张量，窗口只是中转站，结果不驻留；零拷贝路径（`out=` / `empty_output`）结果落在**调用者自己的缓冲**里，天然与别的调用隔离。`tag` 防的那类冲突在这两条路径上都无法构造。（`lend=True` 的轮转是后来为 async 加的第四入口，槽选择由调用计数决定——它面对的同一问题用的是 SPMD 一致量而非 `tag`，见 u4-l4。）

**练习 2**：`reserve()/seal()` 防的死锁「食物被删掉了」是什么意思？

**答案**：[docs/design.md:L205-L208](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/docs/design.md#L205-L208)：旧池的分配是集合的且会做流同步，若发生在一次调用的中途，会与那次调用**故意留在飞行中的自旋屏障**互相等待——屏障等对端、对端等分配、分配等屏障。后来的设计把收尾握手延迟到不再与分配交叠的位置，自旋屏障不再滞留空中，这个死锁失去了食物；分配依旧集合（u4-l1 的 rendezvous 论证），但不再有死锁可喂。

**答案**：因为 peer 的 flag 地址按值装在 `BarPeers::p[8]`（[src/barrier.cu:L27-L29](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/src/barrier.cu#L27-L29)）这个定长数组里随内核参数传入。放宽至少要改成指针+长度（或 `cudaMemcpyToSymbol` 到常量/全局内存），并同步放宽算子层 `[1,8]` 校验；但单节点 8 卡的物理上限让它不值得——这正是「结构事实」类边界与「待办」的区别。

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a listing from the system with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a message from the system confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a message from the system confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.
